title: QBR - Orchid AI Health Check
summary: Quarterly business review and health check focusing on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents over last quarter, and roadmap alignment. Discussed cost optimization levers (batching, quantization), Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for upcoming expansion, and planned benchmarks for private deployment. Agreed on next steps: send updated cost breakdown, schedule benchmark run, and follow up on SOC2 scoping doc.
topics: Pilot Dedicated capacity vs Private deployment
next_steps: Redwood to send month-by-month cost breakdown and per-route latency percentiles
Orchid AI to confirm timeline for Q1 expansion (expected pilot start by 2027-01-15)

Share SOC2 artifact link and kms integration notes

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Voss (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Orchid AI - Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Orchid AI - CTO), Javier Ramos (Orchid AI - SRE)

Summary (auto): QBR / health check. Usage up ~32% q/q, costs creeping due to heavy long-context generation, one reliability incident in Nov due to autoscaler mis-config, evaluating Dedicated vs Private for Q1 pilot.

[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is our qbr slash health check for orchid, appreciate you blocking time
[00:12] Priya Desai: thanks lena, yeah we wanted to go over usage, cost spikes and talk about dedicated pilot, also quick ask on SOC2 artifacts
[00:22] Marcus Voss: quick intro from my side - i'll be owning the bench marks and the technical follow ups, expect some logs and perf traces after the run
[00:30] Ethan Cole: great, real quick context - our customer support flows have doubled token consumption since September, so cost is our top concern, latency is still important but cost first
[00:47] Lena Park: got it. on the usage side we saw 32% q over q increase, mostly XG generation routes, a few routes with high context. i pulled a per-route breakdown before this call
[01:05] Priya Desai: yep those are the conversation generation routes, long histories, we also started doing nightly batch summaries which use a longer seq len
[01:18] Marcus Voss: two quick things we usually recommend - int8 quantization for the ephemeral worker pools and prefix caching for the convo routes. batching is useful but careful with tail latency for live chat
[01:36] Javier Ramos: what about cache invalidation? our sessions update frequently, worried about stale responses if caching aggressive
[01:44] Marcus Voss: absolutely, that's why we do selective prefix/KV caching, not full response caching; you can set TTLs based on session activity. also note our runtime supports partial kv eviction so you don't have to wipe entire context
[02:03] Ethan Cole: last month we had a 4 hour degradation window - what happened there? svc in az-east-2 timed out
[02:13] Lena Park: yes there was an autoscaler mis-config combined with a model fallback that didn't trigger as expected, that caused increased latencies. we've since patched the policy and added an extra fallback route to a lower-cost model for resilience
[02:30] Priya Desai: do you have the postmortem? our security team asked for the incident log and remediation steps
[02:38] Lena Park: i will share the incident doc and the remediation notes, plus the action items we ran. marcus can also attach the perf traces
[02:47] Marcus Voss: i'll include heap / gpu usage and the trace for the autoscaler events, should help your SRE team
[03:00] Ethan Cole: thanks. on Dedicated vs Private - curious about throughput guarantees and pricing model. our legal team is leaning private for the PII flows, but we want to measure economics first
[03:14] Marcus Voss: Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and a committed SKU. Private adds your VPC/on-prem control plane and KMS integrations but has higher setup overhead. for economics we should run the same workload on both to compare tokens per dollar and tail latency
[03:30] Priya Desai: perfect, that benchmark is key. also can you confirm kms/hsm options? we need bring-your-own-kms for some customers
[03:40] Lena Park: yes BYOK supported, we have KMS integrations and can discuss HSM options for private deployments, i'll include the security docs link
[03:50] Javier Ramos: network wise, for private we'll need VPC peering and specific egress rules, i can send topology after this call
[04:00] Priya Desai: cost optimization - can you walk through what drove the spike? was it model size, prompt length, or retries?
[04:10] Marcus Voss: largely prompt length and retries. we saw an uptick in retries for certain intents which multiplied token counts; also some routes were using a larger model than necessary. recommended fixes: smaller model for non-critical routes, request-level dedup and early stop, and smarter batching windows for nightly jobs
[04:35] Ethan Cole: can you quantify savings? if we move 30% of calls to a smaller model and apply int8 quantization, rough estimate?
[04:45] Marcus Voss: ballpark 20-35% cost reduction depending on usage patterns; i'll run model-specific numbers in the benchmark and include in the spreadsheet
[05:00] Priya Desai: there's also a ask about retention - some data needs to be purgeable after 30 days, what options do we have for per-tenant retention?
[05:12] Lena Park: we support configurable retention at route level, plus audit logs and export for compliance. for private you can enforce retention with customer-managed stores
[05:23] Javier Ramos: ok good. one more on observability - latency percentiles per route, and token-level cost attribution, is that ready in the console?
[05:34] Marcus Voss: yes we have per-route dashboards, token breakdowns and tracing hooks. we can add custom traces if you want deeper instrumentation
[05:45] Priya Desai: please add an example dashboard to the shared folder, that will help our ops team
[05:52] Lena Park: noted, will share.
[06:00] [Section: Roadmap & feature requests]
[06:02] Ethan Cole: roadmap - we plan to expand to EU region in Q2; need data residency and lower latency for EU customers. also want model rollouts A/B testing for new prompts
[06:18] Marcus Voss: region-based routing and rollouts are supported; we can help set up canary traffic and automatic fallback if a variant regresses. for EU if you go private we can deploy in your cloud region as well
[06:33] Priya Desai: can we get guardrails for model rollouts? automated rollback on quality regression would be ideal
[06:40] Marcus Voss: we have rollout policies tied to evals and can hook SLO-based rollback on adverse quality metrics, we'll include a template for your evaluation set
[06:52] [00:08:00] Priya Desai: small note - sometimes the transcripts (we use for training) get noisy, any best practices?
[08:07] Marcus Voss: we recommend cleaning prompts, add regex filters for PII, and use smaller context windows for training dumps. also you can enable partial redact in transit
[08:20] [00:09:30] Lena Park: ok let's recap action items and next steps
[09:32] Priya Desai: before that, pricing - will you send an updated spreadsheet with per-model costs and suggested batching/TCO?
[09:40] Lena Park: yes i'll send the pricing spreadsheet.
[09:44] Marcus Voss: i'll run the dedicated vs hosted benchmark with your sample prompts and the planned request distribution, results by 2027-01-10
[09:54] Priya Desai: we'll get you the prompt sets by 2026-12-27 and network topology by 2027-01-05
[10:05] Ethan Cole: SOC2 artifacts? our compliance team needs the scope and evidence
[10:12] Lena Park: i'll share the SOC2 scope doc and evidence links, and we'll loop in security for any follow ups
[10:18] [00:12:00] Javier Ramos: little feed - in the November incident, the log had some mis-typed config names, so if you can standardize naming that'd help
[12:25] Marcus Voss: good call, we'll standardize the scaler/route names in the config bundle we send
[12:33] [00:20:00] Priya Desai: timeline - we are targeting a pilot for Q1 for the EU customers specifically, want to decide between Dedicated and Private by mid-Jan
[20:12] Lena Park: that timeline sounds doable, we'll prioritize the benchmark and cost sheet to help you decide
[20:22] [00:30:00] Ethan Cole: any blockers from your side?
[30:06] Marcus Voss: nothing technical, just need prompt sets and network info from orchid to run the bench, and access to the sample logs.
[30:20] Priya Desai: we'll share a s3 bucket with examples and an access window.
[30:28] Lena Park: great. final recap - send pricing sheet, SOC2 docs, run benchmark, Orchid sends prompts and topology.
[30:40] Priya Desai: thanks everyone, appreciate the partnership.
[30:45] Lena Park: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and calendar invites.

References / Links Mentioned: [pricing spreadsheet link], [SOC2 artifacts link], [benchmark run ticket], [shared dashboard template]

End of transcript.
